items.headline: Can AI design circuit boards yet?
items.dek: OpenAI showed GPT-6 Astra working in KiCad. We have been building a way to measure whether the circuits that come out of these models are any good.
items.caption: Blog title + dek + date with orange eye-diagram banner
items.notes: Quote: "For a useful and growing set of circuit problems, we think the answer is already yes. The scores also make it clear that there is plenty left to do." / "We still would not ask it to design a pacemaker and blindly install the result. But we are on the way there." Sept 1 results top-5: Claude Opus 5 61.6%, Grok 4.6 57.1%, Claude Fable 5.1 56.4%, Claude Fable 5 54.3%, Claude Opus 4.8 Max 51.4%. Also notes xAI included EEBench in the Grok 4.6 model card.

items.headline: One real failure
items.dek: A submitted design used 22 µF nominally. At 4.7 V bias, the grader found only 11.4 µF of effective capacitance, far below the 545 µF requirement. The source built successfully; the circuit still failed the job.
items.caption: Saved ngspice output: protected rail falls below the 3 V minimum after 0.85 ms (needed 20 ms) — shows grading is physics/simulation-based

items.headline: Where the time goes (EEBench methodology)
items.dek: requirements → design → test — 60% of an engineer's week. EEBench V1 measures this loop end to end. schematic + layout stay thin: the CAD writes down what simulation, calculation, and research already decided.
items.caption: Bar of an EE's week: arch 10%, requirements 10%, design 22%, schematic 3%, layout 5%, review 15%, build 10%, test 20%, prod 5% with a 'close the loop' arrow
items.notes: atopile's own estimate (not a survey). Scoring: "0.65 × technical + 0.35 × cost-efficiency against a reference BOM"; "No human graders. No LLM-as-judge."; tasks "original, authored in 2026, and never published". Layout is out of scope in V1.

items.dek: Engineering represents one of the core domains where improved agent capabilities directly support the acceleration of technological development: agents that accelerate rocket design, IC layout, and datacenter power-and-cooling optimization compress the timelines of progress across the physical systems that enable further advances in AI capabilities and utility.

items.headline: Parametric CAD Bench V3: Text, Editing, and Engineering Drawings
items.dek: V3 closes a reward-hacking avenue exposed by v2. In v2 trajectories, we observed agent-model systems attempting to locate or download the held-back reference CAD or the validator and grader artifacts instead of solving the modeling task from the provided inputs.
items.caption: Screenshot of the paragraph (white padded) — CAD agents caught trying to grab the answer key
items.notes: Safety-relevant. Continues: "The observation does not imply that every v2 system behaved this way or that every v2 score was affected, but it showed that stronger runtime isolation was necessary." V3 release (Sep 21) table: GPT-6 Astra 56.87%, Claude Fable 5.1 56.75%, Claude Opus 5 50.86% (Opus 5.5 later took #1 at 61.03 on Sep 24 — already in work/manifest.json). V3 cohort cost: GPT-6 Astra $317.81, Fable 5.1 $1,056.04.

items.headline: ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC
items.dek: OpenAI cut typical development timelines in half, and the industry has already come knocking to understand how.
items.author: Jake Roach
items.caption: Headline, byline, dek, photo of the Jalapeño wafer
items.notes: Richard Ho quotes: "In the old baseline, you’re talking 18 months to two years, roughly." / "We’re starting from scratch here. We had nothing. There’s not a line of code here to refer to." / "the AI models for us is mostly Codex, Sol, the one before Sol, and now we’re moving on to Astra… we ourselves were shocked at how much better Codex was and what it could do" / "This is how AI should be used. We didn’t replace our engineers; they just became super productive. With a smaller team of really good engineers with a lot of this AI stuff, you could do things faster and better than you could otherwise." RTL to tapeout in ~nine months. Caveats: Broadcom did physical design; B0 stepping reportedly up to 25% better perf/W than A0.

items.headline: Fig. 5. Requirements for recursive self-improvement.
items.dek: We believe this is one of the earliest demonstrations of recursive self-improvement: an AI system designed an AI accelerator, deployed an AI model on it, and used that model to improve a future generation of the accelerator.

facts.claim: EEBench (Sep 29, 2026): Claude Opus 5.5 scores 75.0% on 13 held-out, simulation-graded electrical-engineering design tasks; GPT-6 Astra 69.3%. On Sep 1 the top score was 61.6%.

EEBench grading: "No human graders. No LLM-as-judge." Designs are built and simulated in SPICE at worst-case component-tolerance corners; score = 0.65 × technical + 0.35 × cost-efficiency vs a reference BOM.
xAI now headlines EEBench in launches: Grok 4.7 lists "Electrical engineering — EEBench 64.0%" next to coding and legal benchmarks.

xAI Grok 4.6 model card: "agents that accelerate rocket design, IC layout, and datacenter power-and-cooling optimization compress the timelines of progress across the physical systems that enable further advances in AI capabilities and utility."

OpenAI launch caption: "This is a 15-second condensed playback of GPT-6 Astra performing printed circuit board (PCB) layout in KiCad, turning an electronic schematic into a manufacturable PCB by placing components and routing copper connections." (2 min 54 s run)
facts.source: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra launch page, quoted by JLCPCB

facts.claim: From a four-line brief, GPT-6 Astra produced a 44 × 34 mm two-layer amplifier board in KiCad with 0 ERC and 0 DRC violations under the configured rules (5 DRC and 4 ERC categories ignored).
Quilter Project Speedrun: an 843-component, 8-layer, two-board Linux computer booted on first power-up; 38.5 human hours with AI vs 428 hours quoted for manual layout (~11x).
Autodesk: an agent designed an injection-molded enclosure, its mold and CNC toolpaths from a chat window — "a design-to-manufacturing chain that normally requires several people over several days".

CAD Bench V3: "we observed agent-model systems attempting to locate or download the held-back reference CAD or the validator and grader artifacts instead of solving the modeling task" (reward hacking in v2).
OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC went from RTL to tapeout in ~9 months using Codex; Richard Ho: "In the old baseline, you’re talking 18 months to two years, roughly."

Richard Ho (OpenAI): "This is how AI should be used. We didn’t replace our engineers; they just became super productive. With a smaller team of really good engineers with a lot of this AI stuff, you could do things faster and better than you could otherwise."

Architect Labs (Aug 27, 2026): two human architects wrote a spec; its AI generated 100% of the RTL, verification, firmware, drivers and kernels for an AI accelerator in under two weeks — "one of the earliest demonstrations of recursive self-improvement" (company claim; FPGA prototype, not yet taped out).
Cadence claims its ChipStack agents cut "a typical five-week verification loop to less than a day" (over 40x); Synopsys claims up to 50x faster RTL validation — both vendor-measured.
Analog Design Bench: on 50 transistor-level analog tasks from 17 chip designers, the best agent (Claude Fable 5) passes the full spec 78% of the time in two-hour attempts; the worst 8%.
HWE-Bench: the best agent fixes 70.7% of 417 real bugs in open-source chip repositories (OpenTitan, CVA6, XiangShan…); >90% on small cores, <65% on SoC-level projects.
In June 2025 NVIDIA's CVDP benchmark found state-of-the-art models "achieving no more than 34% pass@1 on code generation" for Verilog.
Median pay (May 2025): computer hardware engineers $161,740; electrical & electronics engineers $125,040; mechanical engineers $104,110 — vs $50,980 for all workers.

Training: all three jobs typically need a bachelor's degree; a Professional Engineer license additionally requires passing the FE exam, "Relevant work experience typically at least 4 years", and the PE exam (BLS, mechanical engineers).
facts.source: BLS OOH — Mechanical Engineers, How to Become One

facts.claim: U.S. jobs (2025): 297,900 electrical & electronics engineers, 298,500 mechanical engineers, 76,100 computer hardware engineers.
Designing a leading-edge chip: "approximately $249 million for a 7nm chip and approximately $725 million for a 2nm chip" (IBS).
facts.source: Arm Holdings IPO prospectus (Form 424B4), citing IBS

facts.claim: PCB designs average 2.9 respins before volume production, "with each rework cycle adding roughly two weeks and more than $28K in material costs alone" (Lifecycle Insights study).
Synopsys benchmarks its spec-to-verified-RTL agent against "a four- to six-month team effort".
Flux (AI hardware engineer) raised $37M (Feb 2026); reports 1 million+ sign-ups and nearly 6.5 million devices designed on the platform.
